newsitem.title: USA: Bombay Co sees Q3 hit by Nourse severance.
newsitem.headline: Bombay Co sees Q3 hit by Nourse severance.

text.p: Bombay Co's new chief executive officer warned that third-quarter results could fall short of analysts' expectations because of "excessive" promotions and a big severance package for the company's former management team.
Carson Thompson last week replaced Robert Nourse as president and chief executive officer. Nourse's wife Alexandra, who had been executive vice president of merchandising, was also removed.
In an interview with Reuters on Thursday, Thomspon said the First Call consensus view that Bombay will lose four cents per share in the third quarter was "probably" too optimistic.
"There are other factors dealing with severance pay for the Nourses and the level of promotional activity that we'll be doing ... that will affect that," he said.
"We aren't in a position to be more specific because there are a number of elements of the Nourses' severance agreement that need refinement and finalization," Thompson said.

Thompson said the Nourses had failed to keep up a steady stream of new products in Bombay's traditional business of lower-priced antique reproduction furniture. The company would take several months to get back on track, he said.

Because of a slow rate of introducing products, Bombay relied on "excessive" promotions to drive sales and would have to continue doing so until early next year while it disposes of excessive inventory, he said.
The chief executive said Bombay would turn a profit in the fourth quarter, though it would again lose money in the first half of 1997.
"We realistically cannot expect to be profitable in the first or second quarter of next year unless we get a much greater impact out of our new product stream than I think we can," he said.
Still, Thompson said he expected the company to show solid gains again in the second half of 1997 and beyond.
